explained.headline: Venezuelan opposition leader María Corina Machado returns from exile

happened.text: Venezuelan opposition leader María Corina Machado has returned to Venezuela after spending nearly a year in exile.
During a news conference in Caracas, María Corina Machado urged that presidential elections be held in the country next year.
María Corina Machado thanked United States President Donald Trump and his administration for the January action against former President Nicolás Maduro.

background.text: María Corina Machado is a longtime activist who fled Venezuela by speedboat last December to accept the Nobel Peace Prize in Oslo.
Following the removal of Nicolás Maduro in January, the country has been led by interim President Delcy Rodríguez, who previously served as his vice-president.
The interim government subsequently signed an oil agreement granting favourable terms to the United States.

matters.text: Jesus Renzullo also stated that Washington benefits from the interim government while maintaining the appearance of supporting a transfer of power.
María Corina Machado criticised the recent bilateral oil deal for lacking the transparency desired by Venezuelan society.

uncertain.text: Interim President Delcy Rodríguez assured the nation that elections would take place, but did not specify an exact date.
The sources note that various criminal investigations initiated by Venezuela's judiciary against María Corina Machado have not been formally lifted.
It remains unclear what María Corina Machado plans to do next, although she has previously stated an intention to run for president again if an election were held.

explained.headline: Israeli election leaves Netanyahu and rival short of majority

happened.text: The final vote count in Israel's parliamentary election showed that Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's Likud-led bloc finished with 53 seats, while the anti-Netanyahu bloc led by Gadi Eisenkot claimed 48 seats.

background.text: Gadi Eisenkot, a former military commander, led an opposing coalition of right-wing, centrist and liberal parties aiming to oust the incumbent prime minister.
Arab Israelis, many of whom refer to themselves as Palestinian citizens of Israel, make up about a fifth of the country's population.

matters.text: DW reported that difficult coalition talks are expected in the weeks ahead, and the resulting coalition will largely determine whether Israeli policy in Gaza continues on its current course.

The sources note that the success of Arab parties could give Arab lawmakers unprecedented influence over coalition negotiations, though it remains unclear if these gains will translate into real political power.

uncertain.text: It is still unconfirmed whether the right-wing factions of Eisenkot's anti-Netanyahu bloc would ultimately entertain the possibility of working with the Arab-led parties.
Netanyahu's Likud claimed large-scale foreign involvement involving Qatar and Turkey, but Israeli authorities, police officials and election committee representatives refuted the claims.

removed.text: As at least 61 seats are needed to form a secure majority in the 120-seat Knesset, neither major bloc reached a governing majority.
